heading: Prefix sums answer range queries instantly
body:
Counting vowels in `word[left:right]` character-by-character takes O(N) per query. But if we **precompute** a prefix sum — where `prefix[i]` = vowels in `word[0:i]` — any range becomes:

`prefix[right+1] - prefix[left]`

One O(N) build, then O(1) per query.

heading: Why right+1? Prefix sum indexing
body:
`prefix[i]` counts vowels in `word[0:i]` (up to but NOT including index i).

To include character at index `right`, we need the count **up to** `right+1`.

**Formula:** `prefix[right+1] - prefix[left]` gives vowels in `word[left:right+1]`.

label: Core · Python

q: Why do we use `prefix_sum[right + 1] - prefix_sum[left]` instead of `prefix_sum[right] - prefix_sum[left]`?
options: Because `prefix_sum[i]` stores the count of vowels in `word[0:i]`, so to include index `right`, we need `prefix_sum[right + 1]`.
To avoid off-by-one errors in the loop.
Because `right` is always one less than the actual endpoint.
Because Python uses exclusive end indices in slicing.
explain: `prefix_sum[i]` represents the vowel count in `word[0:i]`, so to include character at index `right`, we need the count up to `right + 1`.
